chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The first thing that is begun with in the Hereafter is the charity of water, meaning regarding the recompense.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Prophet Muhammad or Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the first deed to be judged in the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the preeminent status of *Sadaqat al-Ma'* (charity of water) as the first deed to be accounted for on the Day of Judgment, underscoring its essential role in human survival and spiritual purification. While the chain attributes the statement to the Prophet, Imam al-Sadiq’s narration serves to validate and emphasize this practice within Shia jurisprudence, linking physical sustenance directly to eternal reward. This emphasis reflects the broader Islamic principle that basic necessities, particularly water, carry immense weight in divine reckoning due to their universal utility.
